To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we prove the unique determination of a general vector field depending on both space and time variable, and of a general quasilinear terms appearing in a parabolic equations, from the knowledge of the solutions of the equations on the lateral boundary.

we prove a new result on the unique determination of a general quasilinear term, appearing in the nonlinear parabolic equation ∂tu−∆xu+F(x, t, u(x), xu(x)) = 0, from measurements of the solution on the lateral boundary.

we have developed new methods for solving inverse problems for diffusion equations with convection terms and quasilinearities, in the case of a general expression F (t, x, u, xu), and that our methods are applicable to the case of non-linearities.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the determination of the velocity vector field and the density of a fluid from measurements of solutions of the diffusion equations restricted to the lateral boundaries.
the unique determination, in a weak sense, of the convection term in a diffusion equation and with the unique determination of the quasilinear term in a quasilinear parabolic equation.

the unique recovery of convection terms as well as quasi-linearities appearing inside the domain of a diffusion equation, from measurements of the solution on the lateral boundary, in a rough setting.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we prove the unique determination of the general quasilinear terms appearing in a parabolic equation.

we have solved the unique recovery of the convection term, of the diffusion term and of the quasi-linear term in a diffusion equation from lateral boundary measurements, in a rough setting described by coefficients in Lp (Ω) and Lp (∂Ω).
the inverse problem we consider is uniquely solvable, in a suitable weak sense, for general nonlinear expression F (x,t, u, xu), provided the data is sufficiently regular.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, for a given diffusion coefficient, our result provides a unique recovery of the velocity field, the density and the quasilinear terms appearing in the diffusion equations.
, in the linear case, we recover the density and the velocity field, while in the nonlinear case, the quasilinear terms are uniquely determined.
we have proved a general result for the inverse problem of determining a general expression F (u, xu) appearing inside a diffusion equation, from boundary data, which is a very challenging problem.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in both linear and nonlinear settings, we can uniquely recover the coefficient F in a general form.
the recovery of a general expression F(x, t, u) from boundary measurements of the solution u is possible.
the recovery of the first order coefficient is not possible without some additional assumptions on the second order term.
